描述_ZN: Scroll of "The Old Hall of Firs", modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 86.4 cm in length and 76.4 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "The old fir in the old hall of the West Tianmu Mountains is no less than ten thousand copies. Twenty-three years of autumn trip to the return of memories written by the lingering. Beihong." Inscription: "BAI" white seal.　　Twenty-three years refers to the twenty-third year of the Republic of China (1934), Xu Beihong was 39 years old.　　In August 1934, Xu Beihong returned home from Venice, Florence, Rome, Italy, and Moscow, the former Soviet Union, etc. In September, he led the students of the art department of Nanjing Central University, Sun Duo Ci, Yang Jianhou, Wen Jin Yang, Lin Jiaqi and others to Zhejiang Tianmu Mountain to sketch, despite the strenuous journey. He guided the students carefully while actively working on his creation. The present painting is a sketch of an ancient fir in front of an old temple.　　It is a cleverly conceived drawing that uses contrast and concealment to express the imposing nature of the cedar trees. Instead of directly painting the full view of the fir, a low wall of the old temple is painted in front of it, and the low wall sets off the tallness of the fir. Although the wall obscures the roots of the fir, it expands the space for the viewer's imagination, and subtly enhances the aura of the fir.
